- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after recent spikes in history, then drop sharply — model overshoots followed by underestimation.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: forecasts often revert to historical mean too quickly, missing sustained trends.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, especially when true values are rising or stabilizing.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days of the forecast horizon, then become more conservative — suggesting a lagged adjustment to recent data.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in price drops — often underestimates the depth of declines after a spike.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — forecasts spike in response to minor price fluctuations, then fail to adjust downward.
- Model tends to underestimate the true mean of the 30d history, especially when the true outcome is above the historical average.
- Model exhibits “late correction” bias — corrects too late, often missing the true trend by 5–10 days.
- Model overfits recent data — forecasts are too sensitive to the last 5–7 days of history, leading to overreaction to short-term noise.
